2607.09804.title: Trivial Prompt Reframing Bypasses Safety Guardrails in Googleś MedGemma-4B
2607.09804.paper_summary: Open-weight medical language models are increasingly used as the base of patient-facing and clinician-support applications. Their model cards prohibit specific behaviors -- recommending exact drug dosages, issuing definitive diagnoses, prescribing treatments, adjudicating drug-drug interactions, and advising that emergency care can be skipped -- yet a model card describes intended behavior, not robust behavior. We quantify that gap for MedGemma-4B-it under attacks that require no technical sophistication. We build a fully factorial benchmark of 5 guarded-behavior concepts x 50 deterministically templated questions x 6 lay-accessible attack manners x 3 repetitions (4,500 generations), serve the model locally through Ollama under default sampling, and code every response refuse/hedge/comply with three independent judges (an LLM judge, a transparent regex judge, and an NLI-entailment judge). Under the primary LLM judge the overall Attack Success Rate (ASR, the fraction coded comply) is 38.0%. The two framings that reinterpret the request as legitimate dominate: recasting a question as a "medical board exam" item raises ASR from a 29.0% baseline to 53.1% (+24.0 points), and an appeal to an alleged doctor's authority raises it to 43.7% (+14.7); crude instruction-override prefixes have no significant effect. Robustness is dominated by topic: the drug-interaction guardrail is nearly absent (83.2% ASR) while the emergency-deferral guardrail is strong (4.7%) -- and the authority framing is the only attack that breaches it. We report Wilson confidence intervals, cluster-bootstrap effect sizes, a cluster-robust logistic regression, Cochran's Q, per-manner McNemar tests, and inter-judge reliability (Fleiss' kappa = 0.26); absolute ASR is judge-dependent while the ordering of attacks and topics is not. Our findings motivate stronger deployment-time guardrails for open medical models.
2607.09804.paper_summary_zh: 開放式醫療語言模型越來越多地用作面向患者和臨床醫師支持應用的基礎。<lb/>它們的模型卡禁止特定行為——推薦確切的藥物劑量、發出明確的診斷、開處方、裁定藥物間相互作用，以及建議可以跳過急救護理——然而，模型卡描述的是預期行為，而不是穩健行為。<lb/>我們量化了在不需要技術複雜性的攻擊下，MedGemma-4B-it 的這一差距。<lb/>我們建立了一個完全因子基準，包括 5 個受保護行為概念 x 50 個確定性模板問題 x 6 種易於理解的攻擊方式 x 3 次重複（4,500 次生成），通過 Ollama 在默認取樣下本地服務模型，並由三位獨立評審（LLM 評審、透明正則表達式評審和 NLI 蕴涵評審）對每個回應進行拒絕/模糊/遵從的編碼。<lb/>在主要的 LLM 評審下，整體攻擊成功率 (ASR，編碼遵從的比例) 為 38.0%。<lb/>兩種將請求重新詮釋為合法的框架佔主導地位：將問題重新表述為“醫學考試”項目將 ASR 從 29.0% 的基線提高到 53.1% (+24.0 分)，而對所謂醫生權威的訴求則將其提高到 43.7% (+14.7)；粗略的指令覆蓋前綴沒有顯著影響。<lb/>穩健性受主題主導：藥物相互作用的防護措施幾乎不存在（83.2% ASR），而急救延遲的防護措施則很強（4.7%）——而且權威框架是唯一突破它的攻擊。我們報告了威爾遜置信區間、聚類自助效應大小、聚類穩健邏輯回歸、科克倫的 Q 值、每種方式的麥克尼馬爾檢驗和評審間可靠性（弗萊斯卡帕 = 0.26）；絕對 ASR 依賴於評審，而攻擊和主題的排序則不是。我們的發現促使對開放醫療模型進行更強的部署時防護措施。
2607.09804.author: Avi-ad Avraam Buskila et.al.
